f1.quote: Uniaxial tensile loading applied along specific crystallographic directions (<110>, <1-12>, <-111>)

f2.quote: at varied temperatures (10 K, 300 K, 600 K)

f4.quote: annealing history (heated to 1000 K, held, cooled to 300 K)

f5.quote: Nose-Hoover thermostat for thermal control, 1 fs time step

f6.quote: Yielding is triggered by a sudden stress drop associated with the nucleation of dislocations at vacancy sites.

f7.quote: plastic flow is mediated by Shockley partial dislocations (1/6<112>) generating intrinsic stacking faults (ISF) and extrinsic stacking faults (ESF)

f8.quote: forming HCP-like regions locally without bulk phase change

f9.quote: Elevated temperatures reduce yield strength by intensifying atomic thermal vibrations, facilitating dislocation nucleation and reducing critical resolved shear stress.

f10.quote: Maximum yield stress observed along the <-111> orientation

f11.quote: yield strength decreases with temperature; yield strength shows negligible sensitivity to strain rate

f12.quote: dislocation density increases with strain rate; no FCC-to-BCC transformation or twinning observed.
